findings.title: HITL decision's end_tool_cycle() filtering explanation is inaccurate (conclusion still correct)
findings.location: task2-hitl-decision.md â€” 'Resume re-fires BeforeToolCallEvent â€” verified' bullet
findings.problem: Claims the v1:before_tool_call interrupt id 'survives end_tool_cycle() filtering because it does not start with _AGENT_STREAM_INTERRUPT_ID_PREFIX'. In strands/interrupt.py, end_tool_cycle() KEEPS only ids starting with that prefix (and non-None response) and DROPS everything else, including the before_tool_call id. The real reason the interrupt persists: _handle_tool_execution calls _stop_for_interrupts(...) and returns before the end_tool_cycle() reset (which only runs on the non-interrupt completion path). The design's conclusion (resume returns the stored response) is correct and was verified end to end from source; only the justification is wrong.
findings.fix: Replace the end_tool_cycle() sentence with: the interrupt persists because the interrupt path in _handle_tool_execution calls _stop_for_interrupts(...) and returns before the end_tool_cycle() reset; resume() writes the response onto the stored Interrupt by id, and the replayed BeforeToolCallEvent recomputes the same id and returns that response.

findings.title: jira_update_story PUT body shape stated ambiguously
findings.location: task2-design.md â€” Jira contract table, jira_update_story row
findings.problem: 'body = only provided fields, under the resolved change set' could be read as a wrapped {"changes": {...}} body. The verified mahalo-dock executor sends the bare changes dict (json=params.get('changes', {})), and the mock UpdateStoryRequest expects top-level status/assignee/priority/sprint_id/story_points. A wrapped body would be silently ignored (no-op update).
findings.fix: State explicitly: PUT body is the bare changes dict (top-level fields), not wrapped under a 'changes' key â€” i.e. make_request(..., method='PUT', body=changes). Align the contract table with test-plan item 5.

findings.title: pre-GET seam named as make_request but read module calls it via the _jira_request wrapper
findings.location: task2-design.md â€” Jira contract note on the update-story existence pre-GET
findings.problem: jira_get_story does not call make_request directly; it calls module-private _jira_request(endpoint=...), which calls make_request(settings.jira_url, settings.jira_token, ...). Functionally identical, so correctness is unaffected; the wording over-claims 'the same call'.
findings.fix: Reword to 'issues the same GET jira_get_story makes â€” make_request(...) (the read module reaches it via its private _jira_request helper)'. Calling make_request directly (as the design states) is the cleaner choice since it avoids importing a third private symbol; just fix the wording.
